newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan denies charges of aiding Ugandan rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sudan denies charges of aiding Ugandan rebels.

text.p: Sudan denied charges by Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni that it was aiding Ugandan rebels, Sudanese state television said on Thursday.

The television quoted Minister of Culture and Information al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohammed Kheir, official government spokesman, as saying that Sudan had never given any assistance to Ugandan opposition forces and that Museveni's charges were unjustified.
Museveni on Saturday accused Sudan of aiding the rebel Allied Democratic Forces, which he blamed for grenade attacks that killed nine people in Kampala last week.
"These charges are baseless and they come as part of the continuous escalation from Uganda, which wants to create an enemity with Sudan," the television quoted Kheir as saying.
Kheir also said Sudan was committed to the agreement it reached with Uganda in April to stop media campaigns against each other and to settle their disputes through dialogue.
State television also quoted Kheir as saying that Sudan was eager to put an end to the deteriorating relations between the two countries.
